sentence: This project studies how common cannabidiol use is during pregnancy and describes the pregnancy and birth outcomes linked to it.
This project develops a method to work out how members of a receptor family called metabotropic glutamate receptors become active.
This project tries to improve how images are made so that tumor detection and measuring alpha-emitting therapy agents are more accurate.
This project tests whether bacteriotherapy can help treat lung disease after exposure, using firefighters and murine models.
This project studies how genes control how fetal hemoglobin is spread across red blood cells and why patients with sickle cell disease differ.
This project builds a workflow that measures spatial and time-based omics data to profile drugs during drug discovery.
This project studies targets in a cell pathway in Kaposi sarcoma and lymphoma in the context of HIV infection.
This project studies how serotonin in the brain circuits that control breathing is involved in the respiratory depression caused by fentanyl.
This project studies how a gene tied to coronary artery disease controls the changes smooth muscle cells go through during disease.
This project studies how membrane tethering proteins control the structure of presynaptic terminals through calcium changes inside cells.
This project uses microfluidic devices to read abnormal mRNA in many single cells from acute myeloid leukemia.
This project tests whether immune activation and gene variants of Apolipoprotein L1 together lead to disease, using monocyte cells and primary cell culture models.
This project runs shared omics and imaging assays to describe tumors at the DNA, RNA and protein levels.
This project studies the basic science of gene therapy for blood diseases such as sickle cell disease.
This project maps how microglia, the brain's immune cells, change across brain regions in models of HIV and opioid exposure.
This project studies how the gut microbiome in early-onset rectal cancers differs from the tumor microbiome in other colorectal cancer patient groups.
This project tests a gene editing tool to treat recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, using cells treated outside the body and topical delivery.
This project builds tools that combine imaging, pathology and clinical data to sort breast cancer and prostate cancer patients as low or high risk.
This project uses a high-resolution ultrasound imaging system to study heart disease, cancer and other health conditions in small animal models.
This project studies how epithelial stem cells and regulatory T cells interact to help wounds heal.
